entities.summary: Engineering is a global, Classical-era discipline that utilizes natural science, mathematics, and the engineering design process to solve problems within technology, increase efficiency and productivity, and improve systems. This practice emerged in ancient civilizations, with the earliest recorded evidence of engineering dating back to the Indus Valley Civilization (c. 3300-1300 BCE), where sophisticated irrigation systems and architecture were developed. The discipline gained momentum in ancient Greece, where engineers like Archimedes (c. 287-212 BCE) made groundbreaking contributions to the field, including the development of the screw and the principle of buoyancy. The Romans further advanced engineering, building complex aqueducts, roads, and public buildings that showcased their expertise. Engineering has since evolved to encompass a broad range of specialized subfields, including civil, mechanical, electrical, and chemical engineering, each with its unique emphasis on applications of mathematics and science. Modern engineers continue to push the boundaries of innovation, harnessing advances in technology and science to improve systems, increase efficiency, and productivity, and enhance the human condition.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Engineering has had a profound impact on human civilization, transforming the way we live, work, and interact with one another. From the development of modern civil engineering to the creation of the first practical steam engines, engineering has played a crucial role in shaping the world we know today.
